messages.subject_clean: Updating a ui display from data within the server
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

this should be relatively easy to do, I recently completed a similar project, the difference between what you are doing and what I was doing was user input controlled the way one steppedthrough the simulation. I would write the simulation as a separate function return the needed values and then call this function from within observeEvent this is sort of what you  ar doing in your minimal example anyway.The main difference is that you would need to wrap your loop within a function. Rather than embedding it within observeEvent() directly.

You only really need reactive functions or values if the simulation id dependent on user input.

There is also a question of how you want to display your model on ui, I used tabular output, but have been exploring the possibility of using animation to present graphical output, there appears to be some debate as to whether this is possible or not with Shiny.

R.

Hello,

I have a shiny app on a aws-EC2 instance (r4.xlarge) loading four tables from a database also on aws (postgres).

The app works very well and loads pretty quickly when I run it on the R studio server installed on the same aws-EC2 instance.

But then when I try to visualise the app with http://XX.XXX.X.XXX:3838/my_app/ it does not work and I only get the "An error has occurred The application failed to start. The application exited during initialization."

When I look at the inspect element, I see "Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 500 (Internal Server Error)"

I can make the app work if I reduce the number of rows I pull with `collect(mydata, n = Inf)`. For example, 900000 instead of Inf will work.

I know I can boost the memory of the instance, but I would like to understand why it is working on the r studio server (same memory) but not with http://XX.XXX.X.XXX:3838/my_app/?

I also added this to my shiny-server.conf file with no success.

app_init_timeout 300;

app_idle_timeout 300;

Any suggestions? Did I miss something?

thank you!

Martin

messages.body_plain:
I recently went through the same thing. I ended up wiping my instance and starting over and still had the same issue. After searching for hours, it turned out I was missing an R package. Here's the steps I took to help debug the problem.

1. View the shiny-server.log to see if there's any more detail

sudo cat /var/log/shiny-server.log

2. By default, shiny-server sanitizes errors. Let's fix that.

Open config file

sudo nano /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf

Add this line in your config file (I added it right after the log_dir line)

sanitize_errors false;

3. Restart the shiny server

sudo systemctl restart shiny-server

4. Navigate to xx.xxx.x.xxx:3838/my_app/

You should see the same error ("An error has occurred The application failed to start. The application exited during initialization.") along with a terminal like window. It should have a lot more information on the precise error.

Hope that helps!!

- DCR

messages.subject: Shiny: Help Defining a Custom SliderInput Step set
messages.subject_clean: Shiny: Help Defining a Custom SliderInput Step set
messages.body_plain:
Hi Guys,

I have integrated Shiny with Leaflet, with a working SliderInput. The problem is that there are a lot of values at the lower part of the Sliderinput scale and very few values towards the upper part of the scale.

I have tried using steps of 50 which doesn't seem to work and I would ideally like to go up in steps of (10, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 4000) on the slider bar.

I am asking for help on defining a custom Slider input, with the above steps.

I would be most thankful if someone could help solve this issue,

Kind regards,
Tom.

############################################################
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)
library(leaflet)
library(rgdal)
library(sp)
library(rsconnect)

crime <- readOGR("./crime2017a",layer="crime2017a")
crime <- spTransform(crime, CRS("+init=epsg:4326"))
names(crime) <- c("LSOA","Crime_count","Anti_social_behaviour","Burglary","Violent_crime","Shoplifting","Criminal_damage")

#custom tiles
MBaccessToken <- "X" #removed
MBurlTemplate <- "X=" #removed
MBTemplate <- paste(MBurlTemplate,MBaccessToken,sep="")

ui <- dashboardPage(skin="black",
                    dashboardHeader(title = "Crime Reported in Liverpool 2017", titleWidth = 450),
                    dashboardSidebar(width = 450,
                                     tags$head(
                                       tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", type = "text/css", href = "custom.css"),
                                       tags$script(src = "custom.js")
                                     ),
                                     sidebarMenu(
                                       menuItem("Maps", tabName = "maps", icon = icon("globe")),
                                       menuItem("Charts", icon = icon("map"), tabName = "charts"))
                    ),

                    dashboardBody(
                      sliderInput("range", "Crime Count", min(crime$Crime_count), max(crime$Crime_count),
                                  value = range(crime$Crime_count), step = 50),
                      # Also add some custom CSS to make the title background area the same
                      # color as the rest of the header.
                      tags$head(tags$style(HTML('
                                                .skin-blue .main-header .logo {
                                                background-color: #3c8dbc;
                                                }
                                                .skin-blue .main-header .logo:hover {
                                                background-color: #3c8dbc;
                                                }
                                                '))),

                      leafletOutput("mymap",width="100%",height="1000px"),
                      tabItems(
                        tabItem(tabName = "maps"),

                        tabItem(tabName = "charts")
                      )
                      )
                      )

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  #set slider ranges
  filteredData <- reactive({
    crime[crime$Crime_count >= input$range[1] & crime$Crime_count<= input$range[2],]
  }) #range[1] = min #range[2]= max

  colorpal <- reactive({
    pal <- colorQuantile("YlOrRd", domain = crime$Crime_count, n=8)
  })

  output$mymap <- renderLeaflet({

    #reactive expression represents the palette function,
    # which changes as the user makes selections in UI.

    leaflet(crime) %>%
      addTiles(MBTemplate, options=tileOptions(minZoom=11, maxZoom=18)) %>%
      setView(-2.959761, 53.404049, 11)

  })

  #only elements that are reactive are defined here
  observe({
    pal <- colorpal()

    leafletProxy("mymap", data = filteredData())  %>%
      clearShapes() %>%
      addPolygons(
        fillColor = ~pal(Crime_count),
        fillOpacity = 0.6,
        popup = ~paste(Crime_count),
        color = "#BDBDC3",
        weight = 1)
  })

  observe({
    proxy <- leafletProxy("mymap", data = crime)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
############################################################
